 Wireless charging has taken a major leap forward. The new Qi2.2 standard—also known as Qi2 25W—delivers nearly 70% more power than the original Qi2, bringing true fast-charging speeds to magnetic wireless charging without the cable. For iPhone 17 users, this means 25W wireless speeds that match wired-level charging performance, with active cooling ensuring your device stays safe and efficient.

 What Is Qi2.2 Wireless Charging? A Detailed Breakdown
 To understand Qi2.2, it helps to see how the standard evolved. The Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) introduced the original Qi standard in 2010, establishing a universal foundation for wireless charging. Qi2 arrived in 2023, integrating magnetic alignment technology (Magnetic Power Profile, or MPP) to ensure perfect device-to-charger positioning. Now, Qi2.2—officially released by the WPC in Spring 2025—raises the power ceiling from 15W to 25W and introduces strict thermal requirements.

 How Does Qi2.2 Deliver 25W Wireless Charging?
 Hitting 25W wirelessly isn't just about cranking up the power—it requires a tightly integrated system of hardware and software working in perfect sync. Here's how Qi2.2 actually makes it happen.
 MPP 2.0: Precision That Prevents Waste
 The secret to Qi2.2's speed lies in its Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) 2.0 system. While earlier wireless pads required careful positioning to avoid energy loss, Qi2.2 uses a ring of magnets that snap your iPhone into the exact optimal position—with ±0.5 mm precision.
 This isn't just about convenience—it's about efficiency. When the coils are perfectly aligned, less energy dissipates as heat and more flows directly into your battery. At 25W, even a slight misalignment would cause significant power loss and overheating.
 EDC: The Smart Negotiator
 Extended Data Communication (EDC) is the brain behind the operation. It enables real-time dialogue between your iPhone and the charger, dynamically negotiating voltage and current based on battery level and thermal conditions.
 This isn't a one-size-fits-all handshake—it's a continuous conversation that adjusts power delivery second by second. By enabling real-time thermal monitoring and precise foreign object detection, EDC dynamically regulates power delivery to prevent overheating, ensuring safe and reliable 25W charging at all times.
 The Thermal Challenge—and Why Active Cooling Matters
 At 25W, electromagnetic coil energy loss generates significant heat. Here's the physics problem: electromagnetic coil losses generate heat roughly proportional to the square of the current. Jumping from 15W to 25W doesn't just produce 67% more heat—it can more than double it.
 Without active cooling, the charger's internal temperature would spike, forcing the system to throttle power back to 15W or lower within minutes. That's why Qi2.2 mandates a strict 40°C surface temperature limit—and why the best chargers integrate fans or thermoelectric cooling to sustain full 25W output without compromising safety or battery health.
 That's why the best Qi2.2 wireless chargers integrate built-in fans or thermoelectric cooling systems to sustain peak performance.
 For a deeper dive into what makes a Qi2 charger truly fast, check out our detailed guide: What Makes a Qi2 Wireless Charger Truly Fast for iPhone 17 ?
 What Does Qi2.2 Mean for iPhone 17?
 The iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max all support Qi2.2 25W wireless charging out of the box. In real-world testing, a Qi2.2 25W charger can push an iPhone 17 Pro from 0% to 50% in approximately 22 minutes. Measured data indicates that actual charging power can reach nearly 30W on the iPhone 17 Pro without a case—more than 10W higher than what a Qi2.0 charger delivers under the same conditions.
 With iOS 26, all iPhone 16 and iPhone 17 models (excluding the 16e) unlock full Qi2 25W support. For iPhone 17 Air, speeds max out at 20W.
 For iPhone 17 users, this translates to effortless, "drop-and-go" charging that actually hits the ultra-fast 25W speeds.
 Qi2.2 vs MagSafe: What iPhone 17 Users Need to Know
 With both standards now capable of 25W, iPhone 17 users face a genuine choice. Here's how they actually compare.
 Different Origins, Same Result. MagSafe is Apple's proprietary system, built around its own certification program (Made for MagSafe). Qi2.2, by contrast, is an open industry standard developed by the Wireless Power Consortium. For iPhone 17 users, the practical outcome is identical: 25W wireless charging on the 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max. The difference lies not in speed, but in ecosystem and flexibility.
 Magnet Compatibility Is Fully Interchangeable. Both standards use the same 44-mm magnet ring specification. A Qi2.2 charger snaps onto an iPhone with the same satisfying click as a MagSafe charger—and vice versa. This means you can mix and match accessories without worrying about physical fit.
 Where They Diverge: Ecosystem and Price. MagSafe chargers undergo Apple's strict certification process, which often commands a premium price. Qi2.2 chargers deliver the same magnetic alignment and charging speed but benefit from broader competition across multiple brands, typically at lower price points. Additionally, Qi2.2 chargers work seamlessly with Android devices that support the standard—something MagSafe cannot claim.
 If you're all-in on Apple and prefer first-party polish, MagSafe is a reliable route. But for most iPhone 17 users, Qi2.2 offers the same core experience with greater versatility and better value—especially when building out a multi-device charging setup across home, car, and travel.

Its 45W USB-C port can even charge a MacBook Air. Thanks to SnapCool active cooling, you can charge two devices simultaneously via wireless and wired outputs without any throttling—a unique advantage over competitors.

 The Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station (3-in-1, MagGo, AirCool, Foldable) folds completely flat for easy travel and delivers full 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging, juicing an iPhone 17 Pro to 50% in just 26 minutes. Its AirCool fan reduces heat by 30%, helping maintain stable Qi2 25W charging and preserve battery health. The 3-in-1 design charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously, with ActiveShield 5.0 running over 10 million temperature checks daily to protect your devices.
 Best for Road Trip & Daily Commutes:
 For iPhone 17 users who need fast charging on the road, the Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger (MagGo, AirCool, Pad) is the fastest wireless car charger for iPhones available. It delivers 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging, pushing your iPhone 17 to 50% in just 22 minutes. The locking adjustable clamp and ultra-strong magnetic attachment keep your phone secure even on bumpy roads—tested across eight rugged conditions.
 Conclusion
 Qi2.2 wireless charging represents a genuine breakthrough for iPhone 17 users. With 25W speeds, precision magnetic alignment, and mandatory active cooling, it finally delivers the fast, reliable wireless charging experience that users have been waiting for. Whether you’re at your desk or on the road, Qi2.2 chargers like Anker MagGo 2 Pro Magnetic Power Bank (10K, Qi2 25W, Active Cooling) make it easier than ever to keep your iPhone 17 powered up—without the cable.
 FAQ
 1. What is the difference between Qi2 and Qi2.2 wireless charging?
 Qi2 supports up to 15W, while Qi2.2 (also known as Qi2 25W) raises the maximum to 25W—about 70% faster. Beyond speed, Qi2.2 enforces a stricter 40°C surface temperature limit and refines magnetic alignment precision to within ±0.5 mm. These improvements ensure safer, more efficient charging, reducing energy waste and heat generation during high-power transfer.
 2. Does the iPhone 17 support Qi2.2 25W wireless charging?
 Yes. All iPhone 17 models—the 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max—fully support Qi2.2 25W wireless charging. The iPhone 17 Air is capped at 20W. To unlock the full 25W speed, you must update to iOS 26 or later. Also ensure you use a Qi2.2-certified charger; older Qi2 pads will only deliver up to 15W even with the latest software.
 3. Why is active cooling necessary for Qi2.2 25W charging?
 At 25W, coil energy losses generate substantial heat. Without active cooling, chargers would quickly throttle power to avoid overheating, reducing charging speed to much lower levels. Active cooling—using built-in fans or thermoelectric (TEC) systems—dissipates heat continuously, sustaining the full 25W output while keeping your iPhone's battery temperature within safe operating limits for long-term health.
 4. How fast does Qi2.2 25W charge an iPhone 17 Pro?
 A Qi2.2 25W charger can take an iPhone 17 Pro from 0% to 50% in roughly 22 minutes under typical room-temperature conditions without a case. Third-party lab tests have recorded actual power delivery peaking at nearly 30W, which is over 10W higher than what a Qi2 charger achieves in the same scenario—making it nearly as fast as wired charging.
 5. Do I need a special cable or adapter for Qi2.2 25W charging?
 Yes. To hit the full 25W output, you must use a USB-C cable and a power adapter rated at 45W or higher with Power Delivery (PD) support. Using a lower-wattage adapter will limit charging speed. Many premium Qi2.2 products, like those from Anker, include a suitable 45W adapter in the box for convenience.

 What is wireless charging? 
 Why wireless charging? ﻿ 
 Is wireless charging safe? 
 Wireless Charger FAQ
 How does wireless charging work?
 Wireless phone chargers is a way to charge your phone without needing to plug it in with a cable. You place your device on a charging pad or stand, and it will start charging automatically using an electromagnetic field. A chip controls the charging process to ensure it's safe and doesn't damage your device. Learn more about how it works here .
 Is wireless charging bad for a battery?
 Neither magnetic charging nor wireless chargers are particularly bad for batteries. A battery slowly wears as it is charged or discharged over time. Leaving devices always charging can be harmful to their batteries. It's recommended to unplug the device once it is charged. Learn more about safety here .
 What phones have wireless charging?
 Apple iPhone: every iPhone since iPhone 8 (2017), including iPhone Air, iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max. iPhone 12 and later add MagSafe magnetic alignment . iPhone 16 and later support Qi2 25W speeds on a Qi2 25W certified charger.
 Samsung Galaxy: every Galaxy S series flagship from S6 onward (S6 through S26), every Galaxy Note from Note 5 on, and the Galaxy Z Fold and Z Flip foldables. The S25 and S26 series support native Qi2 charging. The S26 Ultra reaches 25W with a Qi2 25W charger (S26+ at 20W, S26 at 15W).
 Google Pixel: Pixel 3 through Pixel 10 series, including Pro and Pro XL variants. Pixel 10, 10 Pro, and 10 Pro Fold add built-in Qi2 magnets. Pixel 10 Pro XL reaches 25W on a Qi2 25W charger.
 Other Android: OnePlus 13 and HMD Skyline support Qi2 at 15W. Most other Qi-enabled Androids work at 5-7.5W on a standard Qi pad.
 How do I use a wireless charger pad?
 To use a wireless charger pad, first plug it into a power source and place your compatible device on the pad, making sure it's centered and aligned with any guidelines provided. Wait for the charging process to start, which may be indicated by a light or other indicator. It's important to note that not all devices are compatible with all wireless chargers, so check your device's specifications to ensure compatibility with the charger and the charging standard. 
 How do wireless charging pads work?
 Wireless charger pads use a technology called inductive charging to transfer energy wirelessly from the charger to the device being charged. This works through two coils, one in the charger and one in the device, that create an electromagnetic field. Most wireless chargers use Qi, MagSafe, Qi2, or the newer Qi2 25W standard. Compatibility, charging speeds and other features vary based on the wireless charging technology.
 How do wireless charging stands work?
 Wireless charging stands are similar to charging pads, but hold the device at an angle so it can be viewed while it charges. They work by using inductive charging, which transfers energy wirelessly from the charger to the device being charged. The charger contains a coil of wire that creates an electromagnetic field, and the device being charged contains a coil that picks up this field to charge the battery. Charging stands use the Qi, MagSafe, Qi2, or Qi2 25W standard. Qi2 and MagSafe stands add magnetic alignment for iPhone 12 and later; Qi2 25W stands reach 25W on iPhone 16 and later.
 Does my iPhone have wireless charging?
 Yes, every iPhone from iPhone 8 (2017) onward supports wireless charging. The wattage and standard depend on the model:
 iPhone 8 through 11 series: Qi at up to 7.5W
 iPhone 12 through 15 series: MagSafe at up to 15W
 iPhone 16 and later: up to 25W on a Qi2 25W certified charger
 iPhone Air: up to 20W on a Qi2 25W certified charger
 For maximum speed on iPhone 16 and later, use a Qi2 25W certified charger like Belkin's Magnetic Charger with Qi2 25W . For more, see our iPhone 17 fast charging guide .
 Does my Samsung phone have wireless charging?
 Yes, most Samsung Galaxy phones since the Galaxy S6 (2015) support wireless charging. Coverage by series:
 Galaxy S series: S6 through S26 (S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, S20, S21, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26 and their Plus / Ultra variants)
 Galaxy Note series: Note 5, 8, 9, 10, 10+, 20 5G, 20 Ultra 5G
 Galaxy Z foldables: Z Fold, Z Fold2, Z Fold3, Z Fold4, Z Fold5, Z Fold6; Z Flip, Z Flip 5G, Z Flip3, Z Flip4, Z Flip5, Z Flip6
 Galaxy A series: select higher-end models (A80, A90, A91)
 The Galaxy S25 and S26 series support the Qi2 magnetic profile natively. The S26 Ultra reaches 25W with a Qi2 25W certified charger; S26+ reaches 20W; S26 reaches 15W. Earlier Galaxy phones charge wirelessly but need a Qi2-ready case for snap-on magnetic alignment.
 For more, see our Qi2 compatible devices guide .
 Does Android phone have wireless charging?
 Yes, most flagship Android phones from 2018 onward support wireless charging. Coverage by brand:
 Google Pixel: Pixel 3 through Pixel 10 series, including Pro and Pro XL variants. Pixel 10, 10 Pro, and 10 Pro Fold have built-in Qi2 magnets; Pixel 10 Pro XL reaches 25W on a Qi2 25W charger.
 Samsung Galaxy: S6 through S26 (S series), Note 5 through Note 20 Ultra, Z Fold and Z Flip foldables. The S25 and S26 series support Qi2; the S26 Ultra reaches 25W on a Qi2 25W charger.
 OnePlus: OnePlus 8 Pro and later, including OnePlus 13 which supports Qi2 at 15W.
 HMD: HMD Skyline supports Qi2 at 15W.
 Xiaomi: Mi 11, Mi 11 Ultra, 13 Pro, 14 Pro, and 15 series support wireless charging.
 Sony: Xperia 1 II through Xperia 1 VI support wireless charging.
 For maximum wireless speed on Android, use a Qi2 25W certified charger with a Galaxy S26 Ultra or Pixel 10 Pro XL. For more, see our Qi2 compatible devices guide.
 iPhone wireless charger vs. Samsung wireless charger
 The main differences between iPhone and Samsung wireless chargers come down to the wireless standard, the maximum charging speed, and the magnetic alignment.
 1. Wireless standard
 iPhone: Qi (iPhone 8-11), MagSafe (iPhone 12 and later), Qi2 25W (iPhone 16 and later, plus iPhone Air)
 Samsung: Qi (Galaxy S6 through S24), Qi2 (Galaxy S25 and S26 series), Qi2 25W (Galaxy S26 Ultra)
 2. Maximum charging speed
 iPhone: up to 7.5W on Qi, 15W on MagSafe, 25W on Qi2 25W (iPhone 16 and later; iPhone Air caps at 20W)
 Samsung: up to 15W on most flagships, 25W on Galaxy S26 Ultra with a Qi2 25W certified charger (S26+ at 20W, S26 at 15W)
 3. Magnetic alignment
 iPhone: built-in MagSafe magnets on iPhone 12 and later
 Samsung: built-in Qi2 magnets on Galaxy S25 and S26 series; earlier Galaxy phones need a Qi2-ready case for snap-on magnetic alignment
 4. Cross-brand compatibility
 Most modern Qi2 and Qi2 25W chargers work for both iPhone and Samsung. A single Qi2 25W certified charger delivers the fastest available wireless speed on both an iPhone 16 and later and a Galaxy S26 Ultra. For more, see how MagSafe and Qi2 compare .

 Qi (standard): up to 7.5W on iPhone, up to 10W on Samsung
 MagSafe: up to 15W on iPhone 12 and later
 Qi2: up to 15W on iPhone 12 and later, Galaxy S25/S26, Pixel 10, OnePlus 13, HMD Skyline

 Qi2 Wireless Chargers FAQ
 What is Qi2 wireless charging?
 Qi2 wireless charging is the next generation of the Qi standard, developed by the Wireless Power Consortium. It introduces significant upgrades, notably the Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) inspired by Apple's MagSafe technology. This innovation ensures precise alignment between devices and chargers, enabling faster charging speeds up to 15W and seamless compatibility across Qi2-compatible devices. Learn more about Qi2 wireless charging .
 How Does Qi2 wireless charging work? 
 Qi wireless charging uses electromagnetic induction between two coils -- one in the charging pad and one in the device -- to transfer power wirelessly. The pad generates a magnetic field when powered, which induces a current in the device's coil, charging its battery. Proper alignment and Qi certification ensure efficient and standardized charging across compatible devices, offering convenience without the need for cables. Learn more here .

 Is MagSafe the same as Qi2 charging?
 MagSafe and Qi2 are both wireless charging technologies that use magnets to enhance charging efficiency and speed. Qi2 is the latest generation of the Qi standard, which is a universal wireless charging standard for mobile devices. While MagSafe is exclusively available for Apple users, Qi2 is compatible with a wide range of brands. Learn more here. 
 Is Qi2 wireless charging better than MagSafe?
 Qi2 is the latest open wireless charging standard and functions similarly to MagSafe. It is already supported on Samsung Galaxy S25 / S26, Google Pixel 10, OnePlus 13, and HMD Skyline, making it a more universal choice across brands. With Qi2 25W (also called Qi2.2), supported devices can charge at up to 25W — the same maximum offered by Apple's fastest wireless ecosystem. Learn more here .
 Is Qi2 wireless charging compatible with MagSafe?
 Qi2 wireless charging is a separate charging technology that functions similar to MagSafe. However, Qi2 is not MagSafe. Given their similarities, Qi2 products may claim to be MagSafe compatible but it is important to check that your device is Qi2 certified.
 What are the features of Qi2 wireless charging?
 Qi2 offers three core features: magnetic alignment for a secure snap-on connection, fast wireless charging up to 15W on the original Qi2 spec and up to 25W on the newer Qi2 25W (Qi2.2) spec, and universal compatibility across iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, OnePlus, and HMD devices.
 What is the difference between Qi and Qi2 wireless charging?
 Qi tops out at 7.5W on iPhone and 10W on most Samsung phones, with no built-in magnetic alignment. Qi2 adds the Magnetic Power Profile (magnetic snap-on alignment) and raises the maximum to 15W. Qi2 25W (also called Qi2.2) is the newest revision, raising the maximum to 25W on iPhone 16 and later, Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Pixel 10 Pro XL.
 Is Qi2 wireless charging magnetic?
 Yes. If a product claims to be Qi2 certified it will utilize magnets.
 What is the max power of Qi2 wireless charging?
 The Qi2 25W spec (also called Qi2.2) tops out at 25W on iPhone 16 and later (iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max), Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Google Pixel 10 Pro XL.
 A 20W tier covers iPhone Air and Galaxy S26+. Most other Qi2 phones (iPhone 12-15, Galaxy S25 / S26 / S26+, Pixel 10 / 10 Pro / 10 Pro Fold) charge at up to 15W on a Qi2 charger.
 The original Qi2 spec tops out at 15W.
 How to use a Qi2 wireless charger?
 To use a Qi2 charger, simply place the center back of your Qi2-enabled smartphone against the charging pad. The magnetic function of the charger and phone will create a sturdy hold. Once the Qi2 charger is plugged in, it will immediately start charging your phone.
 Does Qi2 25W cause my phone to overheat?
 Faster wireless charging generates more heat, and heat can trigger thermal throttling that slows charging and adds wear to the battery over time.
